proposition: Melvin-Koushki holds that the self-image in Ibn Turka's apologies, produced under great duress, is hardly reflective of his primary concerns; he nonetheless builds Chapter 1's biography primarily on the apologies together with Judi-Niʿmati's account, and calls Fujii Morio's Persian examination of the apologies 'rather unsatisfactory'.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, in the apologies (Nafsat al-Masdur)
mediation.note: Written to the ruler judging him; MK: produced under great duress.
MK's judgement of how far the apologies reflect his concerns is itself part of his argument against the orthodox-Sunni-Sufi reading.
